prerequisites: It is recommended to have completed the subjects corresponding to the BASIC TRAINING modules.
It is recommended to have completed the subjects corresponding to the second year of the INDUSTRIAL BRANCH COMMON module.
It is also recommended to have completed the subject THEORY OF STRUCTURES AND INDUSTRIAL CONSTRUCTIONS from the MECHANICAL SPECIFIC TECHNOLOGY module.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to draft, sign and develop industrial engineering projects concerning the construction, reform, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly or operation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, industrial installations and plants, and manufacturing processes.
Ability to manage the activities subject to the engineering projects described in the previous section.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity and critical reasoning.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Ability to manage specifications, regulations and mandatory standards.
Ability to apply quality principles and methods.
Honesty, responsibility, ethical commitment and spirit of solidarity.
Ability to work in a team.
Ability to know, select, criticize and use diverse sources of information.
Knowledge and use of the principles of material strength.
Knowledge and abilities to organize and manage projects. Know the organizational structure and functions of a project office.
Knowledge and abilities to apply graphic engineering techniques.
Knowledge and abilities to apply the fundamentals of elasticity and material strength to the behavior of real solids.
Knowledge and ability for the calculation and design of structures and industrial constructions.
Knowledge and abilities for the application of materials engineering.
Applied knowledge of manufacturing systems and processes, metrology and quality control.
Perform a topographical survey on site, as well as carry out the basic operations corresponding to the setting out of points and alignments.
Know the most important properties of the materials most used in construction, with special emphasis on concrete and mortars.
Proportion concrete.
Plan and execute the basic operations for setting out an engineering project.
Know the procedures used in earthworks, the design and construction procedures for shallow and deep foundations, as well as the techniques used in ground improvement.
Know the most common procedures used in the construction of steel and concrete structures.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1. Introduction. The Work, Organization and Installations.
Topic 3. Manufacturing, Transport and Placement of Concrete.
teaching_methods: Expository theory classes and board practices (combining theoretical content with problem-solving and exercises)
Classroom practices (discussion and practical activities in the classroom)
Laboratory practical classes (in labs, computer rooms, and open field)
Group tutorials (programmed follow-up activities to guide autonomous learning and supervised work)

assessment_methods.method: Final exam on all topics developed during the course
Evaluation of practices developed during the course

assessment_rules: To pass the course, a grade higher than 5 must be obtained. The written exam grade must be at least 4 points. Evaluation in extraordinary calls will consist of a written exam, where 25% of it may correspond to the practical part. Differentiated evaluation will consist of a written exam, where 30% of it will correspond to the practical part.
